blocks.text: The chapter presents restoration as a whole pattern of life: God dwelling in Jerusalem, older people living long enough to sit in its streets, children playing there, scattered people returning, fruitful fields, truthful public judgment, and mourning fasts becoming joyful feasts. The closing picture widens the horizon further, with peoples from many nations seeking God in Jerusalem. Together these images describe a city marked by security, integrity, celebration, and recognized divine presence.

Verses 9–13 contrast earlier insecurity and unproductive labor with the promised “seed of peace,” fruitfulness, increase from the ground, and dew from heaven. A related retrospective in Haggai recalls diminished harvests—grain, wine, vines, fig trees, pomegranates, and olives—along with blight, mildew, and hail before announcing blessing. This background makes Zechariah’s agricultural language more concrete: the promise concerns a reversal of conditions remembered as scarcity and loss.
